news_drafts.headline: Edinburgh's plan shows a £14.3m gap for 2027/28, rising to £93.0m cumulatively by 2030/31
news_drafts.lead:
The City of Edinburgh Council's medium-term financial plan forecasts a budget shortfall of £14.3m in 2027/28. The cumulative funding gap, excluding the Edinburgh Integration Joint Board (EIJB), which runs health and social care, rises to £47.3m in 2028/29, £70.8m in 2029/30 and £93.0m by 2030/31. The council's update to the plan, set out in February 2026, is in the papers for its meeting on 29 October.

A budget strategy progress update restates the 2027/28 gap from the June 2026 update. It says projections for later years are unchanged pending the Scottish Budget. The gap includes additional sums set aside for contract and other non-pay inflation, and the paper says there remains a risk around the adequacy of that provision. The council's external auditor says the council has developed medium and longer-term financial plans and that the plan shows it is financially sustainable in the short term. Its Exhibit 7 states: "There remain significant risks around long-term borrowing and funding gaps".

The council's share of the EIJB's projected gaps is shown separately: £19.7m in 2027/28, rising to £91.4m in 2030/31. Combined with the council's own gap, the total reaches £184.4m in 2030/31. The council's baseline planning assumption is that "the EIJB will address its own budget gaps without additional" council funding. It does not consider the EIJB's future pressures when developing savings plans, but says it will monitor any risk of overspend that could require additional council funding.

news_drafts.headline: Edinburgh: £4m empty-home premium for housing would raise 2027/28 funding gap from £14.3m to £18.3m
news_drafts.lead:
Dedicating £4m of new council tax income from second and long-term empty homes to housing projects would raise the City of Edinburgh Council's funding gap for 2027/28 from £14.3m to £18.3m. That is according to a report to its Policy and Sustainability Committee, which met on 20 October 2026. The gap is the further savings the council has still to find for that year, which the report calls its "incremental funding gap".

The money comes from the premium, an extra charge added to council tax on those homes. The report says the council had already assumed the new premium income when it set its 2026/27 budget, and estimates it at £4m in 2027/28. Dedicating it to new housing spending means it is not available to close the gap, which widens by the full £4m.

The report's wording is that "introducing new commitments in the way suggested in the motion would add up to £4m to the Council's incremental funding gap in 2027/28". The paper is headed "Application of Second and Long-Term Empty Home Council Tax Premium Income".

news_drafts.headline: Edinburgh forecasts £8.615m council-wide overspend at month three; levy-funded culture projects face December review
news_drafts.lead:
The City of Edinburgh Council is projecting an overspend of £8.615m across all its services for 2026/27, according to the month-three budget monitoring report (the in-year check of spending against budget) before the Culture and Communities Committee on 8 October. The figure was first reported to the Finance and Resources Committee on 24 September, and the paper says "an overall overspend of £8.615m is projected".

Within the committee's own area, Parks and Greenspaces is forecasting spending of £0.203m more than its £7.706m budget. The paper attributes this to "additional transport charges and the cost of temporary toilet facilities". Both are running costs rather than a rise in demand or a fall in income.

A separate paper on the Edinburgh Visitor Levy Cultural Programming Fund sets out how that money will be managed. The council will carry out an income review in December 2026, comparing the levy revenue actually collected with projections. If income is lower, the paper says, "a review will be undertaken of the remaining planned expenditure of the financial year to determine whether there is the requirement to pause projects or reduce the financial allocation". In the meantime, projects in the first year are being programmed quarterly ahead of that review.

findings.headline: Digital Transformation's latest anticipated completion moves from March 2029 to March 2030, marked "Delayed", with £(5.000)m reprofiled.
findings.detail: The approved budget of £5.000m is reduced by the 2025/26 reprofiling of £(5.000)m, leaving a revised budget of £3.000m. Actual spend to month 3 is nil.
findings.matters: A one-year completion slip on a corporate digital programme is a delivery change that a finance director or peer council tracking similar programmes would notice.
findings.figures: Approved budget £5.000m; reprofiling £(5.000)m; revised budget £3.000m; completion moved from March 2029 to March 2030

findings.paper_title: Item 7.6 - Month 3 2027-27 Capital Monitoring and 2026-36 Revised Capital Budget - Appendices
findings.headline: The Specific Capital Grants - TMDF revised budget is £66.383m, after £32.383m of additional in-year funding on a £34.000m approved budget.
findings.detail: Appendix 2 defines additional funding as ringfenced funding received in year for specific use. The table also shows TMDF at £34.000m a year from 2027/28 through 2035/36.
findings.matters: A finance officer at another council would want to know the scale of the grant increase and whether the same ringfenced funding is expected to recur.
findings.figures: Approved £34.000m; additional funding £32.383m; revised £66.383m; £34.000m a year from 2027/28 to 2035/36 (total £372.383m)

findings.paper_title: Item 7.6 - Month 3 2027-27 Capital Monitoring and 2026-36 Revised Capital Budget - Appendices
findings.headline: The Fountainbridge HRA project is marked "Delayed", with £(13.050)m reprofiled and a latest anticipated completion of March 2030.
findings.detail: The revised 2026/27 budget falls from £13.507m at budget setting to £0.515m, with actual spend to month 3 of £0.014m. The paper also marks Meadowbank as "Delayed" with a March 2030 completion, after a reprofiling of £(21.944)m.
findings.matters: Large HRA reprofiling and slippage in the same programme show how a peer council's housing delivery timetable has moved.
findings.figures: Approved budget £13.507m; reprofiling £(13.050)m; revised budget £0.515m; actual to month 3 £0.014m; completion March 2030. Meadowbank reprofiling £(21.944)m

findings.paper_title: Item 7.6 - Month 3 2027-27 Capital Monitoring and 2026-36 Revised Capital Budget - Appendices
findings.headline: The HRA balance to be funded through Loans Fund Advance rises from £115.360m in 2026/27 to £566.075m in 2028/29.
findings.detail: The HRA capital expenditure budget grows from £159.466m in 2026/27 to £641.437m in 2028/29. The balance is then shown falling to £236.855m in 2030/31.
findings.matters: The scale and timing of HRA borrowing through Loans Fund Advance affect both the funding needs and debt position of a peer council's housing programme.

findings.paper_title: Item 7.6 - Month 3 2027-27 Capital Monitoring and 2026-36 Revised Capital Budget - Appendices
findings.headline: The Total Capital Financing Requirement is projected to rise from £2,795.9m in 2025/26 to £5,677.4m in 2030/31.
findings.detail: Gross debt is shown rising from £2,489.8m to £5,381.1m over the same period. The paper reports the difference between gross debt and the CFR in its prudential indicator table.
findings.matters: Growth in the CFR of more than double over five years is a central figure for any lender assessing a council's future borrowing requirement.
